subject: Cognitive Science
title: Synaptic Pruning
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Synaptic Pruning.

hook.text: A toddler's brain has twice as many connections as an adult's. Growing up means losing synapses.

buildup.text: Synaptic pruning eliminates weak connections. It peaks in adolescence, following "use it or lose it."

discovery.text: Surviving connections get myelinated—wrapped in insulation that speeds signals up to 100 times.

twist.text: Pruning moves from back to front. The prefrontal cortex—impulse control—is literally last to finish.

climax.text: This explains impulsive teens: emotional circuits are mature while the braking system is still building.

quiz.question: What does synaptic pruning do?
options: Removes weak neural connections to improve efficiency
